findings.evidence: Homeomorph.toHomotopyEquiv (Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/Equiv.lean:75); equivOfHomotopyEquiv functor = `map hequiv.toFun` (InducedMaps.lean:85-91); Functor.FullyFaithful.mulEquivEnd : End X ≃* End (f.obj X) (Endomorphism.lean:189); FundamentalGroup X x := End (FundamentalGroupoid.mk x) (FundamentalGroup.lean:35) and map's functor sends ⟨x⟩ ↦ ⟨e x⟩ (Basic.lean:302-306).
findings.fix: Define `mulEquivOfHomeomorph e x := (FundamentalGroupoidFunctor.equivOfHomotopyEquiv e.toHomotopyEquiv).fullyFaithfulFunctor.mulEquivEnd ⟨x⟩` (modulo the standard πₓ(.of X)/FundamentalGroupoid X identification), derive the basepoint-adjusted mulEquivOfHomeomorphOfEq by an eqToIso/MulEquiv transport, and prove the `_apply` simp lemmas from FundamentalGroup.map/mapOfEq_apply. This removes mapOfEq_comp, mapOfEq_id, mapOfEq_congr, and mapOfEq_mapOfEq. If the mapOfEq form is required downstream, keep only the `_apply` bridge lemma and drop the manual invertibility scaffolding.
findings.issue: mulEquivOfHomeomorph (and hence mulEquivOfHomeomorphOfEq) is built manually from mapOfEq round trips, forcing the auxiliary lemmas mapOfEq_comp (55), mapOfEq_id (66), mapOfEq_congr (78), mapOfEq_mapOfEq (85). Mathlib already supplies the whole construction: FundamentalGroupoidFunctor.equivOfHomotopyEquiv (Mathlib/.../FundamentalGroupoid/InducedMaps.lean:85) turns a homotopy equivalence into an equivalence πₓ(.of X) ≌ πₓ(.of Y), and Functor.FullyFaithful.mulEquivEnd (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Endomorphism.lean:189) turns the equivalence's fully-faithful functor (Equivalence.fullyFaithfulFunctor, Equivalence.lean:557) into End ⟨x⟩ ≃* End ⟨e x⟩, i.e. FundamentalGroup X x ≃* FundamentalGroup Y (e x). The composition/identity round-trip laws you re-prove are exactly the functor laws (FundamentalGroupoid.map_id / map_comp) that this machinery already consumes.

summary: The homeomorphism → π₁ isomorphism is genuinely new (not in Mathlib or TauCeti), but the ~90 lines of hand-rolled functoriality scaffolding re-derive machinery Mathlib already provides: a homeomorphism is a homotopy equivalence, and Mathlib turns that into an equivalence of fundamental groupoids and then a MulEquiv of vertex (fundamental) groups.
